analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. It makes three edits: the 'Last updated' date (head line 3), the recurrent checkpoint bank gate row (head line 295), and a new paragraph at head lines 300-306 on `alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks`. The row and paragraph add the plain unpublished Nemotron Super owner (`NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache`) to the opt-in resident recurrent bank. The paragraph says its tiled prefill is captured only at multiples of the fixed prefill chunk reached by whole chunks. No code, policy, key handling or coordinator contract changes in the supplied evidence.

Relevant threats: T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle) and A-001. The docs keep the existing safeguards: the bank is opt-in via DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1, bound to the loaded model instance and cacheSalt, writes nothing to disk, and requires verified identity before advertising routing evidence. The resident bank is already described as outside the SSD at-rest crypto and as a same-account TTFT oracle under SEC-035. Adding another model family to that opt-in path does not widen the accepted-risk scope in a way the supplied text contradicts.

Assumption not verified: the actual Nemotron Super implementation, `supportsRecurrentCheckpointReuse` gating and `alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks` code are not in the supplied evidence. The doc claims bit-for-bit continuation, but the evidence cannot confirm it. The next pass should check the code if one is supplied. Docs-only, so no concrete regression is shown.
